summary: Autoscaler stickiness during overlapping cold-starts causing gradual p99 latency rise for dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Over the 2026-03-12 morning peak, customers on a reserved dedicated GPU pool experienced a slow but persistent p99 latency increase (from ~700ms to ~2.6s) and sporadic 5xx attach errors. Impact: customer-facing routes (primarily short streaming chat calls) degraded for multiple tenants in the affected pool. Root cause unknown; initial evidence points at autoscaler 'stickiness' when many small cold-starts overlap with a backend sidecar that delays heartbeat emissions, preventing timely GPU attach decisions.

Environment: production reserved pool: dedicated-cluster-07 (prod-us-east), affected routing group: dp-tier-3, time window: 2026-03-12 09:20-10:40 UTC.

High-level symptoms: gradual p99 increase over ~80 minutes, increase in attach backoff events, autoscaler did not add capacity promptly, batcher queues elongated, and short streaming calls blocked longer than expected. No global control-plane outage noted.

Customer impact: two enterprise customers reported intermittent timeouts and elevated tail latency; one customer (FinEdge Analytics) hit their SLO and opened support escalation.
impact: Multiple enterprise tenants on Dedicated (reserved) pool experienced elevated p99 latencies and intermittent 5xx attach errors causing degraded user experience and a missed SLA for FinEdge Analytics.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate high concurrency of short streaming chat sessions (1000 qps of short streams, average duration 300-500ms) to a single pinned model route on dedicated-cluster-07
Trigger a simultaneous small fleet restart of allocator sidecars (simulate 15-20% churn) to reproduce delayed heartbeat emissions
Observe autoscaler decisions and GPU attach logs for 30-120 minutes after spike start
observed_metrics: p50 stable ~220ms, p95 rose modestly from 420ms -> 680ms, p99 climbed from ~700ms -> ~2600ms over 80 minutes
attach_backoff_count increased 12x compared to baseline (baseline ~5/min -> peak ~60/min)
autoscaler_scale_events: only 1 scale-up during the window, with decision delay ~11 minutes after threshold breach
pool_free_slots dropped below 12% for sustained 20 minutes
batch_queue_length correlated with p99 rise (queue depth grew from 3->18)
sidecar_heartbeat_latency spike from median 120ms -> 1.8s during the incident window
initial_actions: Routed affected customers to hosted fallback model routes (non-dedicated) to restore customer-facing latency within 8 minutes
Increased autoscaler aggressiveness for dedicated-cluster-07 (temporary policy override to lower cooldown and increase max burst) at 09:55 UTC
Enabled additional logging for allocator attach path and sidecar heartbeats
investigation_notes: 09:34 UTC: Observed correlated spike in sidecar heartbeat emission latency across ~40% of nodes in dedicated-cluster-07
09:40 UTC: Query of /var/log/allocator/attach shows repeated ECONNRESET and gRPC deadline exceeded errors while performing GPU handshake
Checks on node-level telemetry show nvlink/driver errors were NOT present; driver logs clean
Autoscaler decision logic: hysteresis threshold not crossed early because scale metrics sampling window missed transient queue growth due to telemetry delay from sidecar

Hypothesis: overlapping cold-starts (many short lived streams causing frequent KV cache misses + sidecar restarts) combined with delayed heartbeats caused the autoscaler to under-react (stickiness), leading to slow scale-up and allowing queue depth to grow and p99 to rise

Runbook checks: no scheduled maintenance, no known fleet upgrades in the region; ephemeral sidecar restarts tied to a nightly deploy rollback attempt that was still gradually rolling back into morning hours
Cross-references: Slack thread #support-dedicated (link) and an internal incident stub INT-2201 about sidecar flaky restarts (linked below)
mitigation: Temporary routing to hosted fallback models applied for affected tenants
Autoscaler cooldown overridden and burst target temporarily increased for dedicated-cluster-07
Restarted allocator sidecar on 6 impacted nodes to flush heartbeat timers; this reduced heartbeat latency spikes after ~12 minutes
next_steps: Postmortem deep dive scheduled with Serving Runtime + Autoscaler + Sidecar teams on 2026-03-15
Instrument autoscaler to consider sidecar heartbeat latency as an input to scale decisions (proposal PR referenced)
Add an alert for sustained heartbeat latency > 800ms across >20% of nodes to trigger preemptive autoscale policy changes
Follow up with FinEdge Analytics customer with RCA and compensation note
comments: 2026-03-12T09:52Z - Diego Ramos: Temporary routing to hosted fallback applied for FinEdge; monitoring for p99. Noticed sidecar heartbeat lag on multiple nodes.
2026-03-12T10:08Z - Aisha Patel: Autoscaler cooldown lowered and burst capacity increased; small improvement in queue depth after ~12m.
2026-03-12T11:20Z - Priya Nair (SRE): Restarted allocator sidecars on 6 nodes; heartbeat latency returned to normal and p99 trended back toward baseline.
2026-03-13T09:05Z - ML Infra (note): Added verbose attach path logs and a temporary metric for heartbeat-emission-latency; planning a tuning PR for autoscaler hysteresis.
resolution: Workaround and mitigation applied: affected tenants routed to fallback and autoscaler temporary policy change; sidecar restarts removed immediate heartbeat lag. Root-cause fix pending: autoscaler should incorporate heartbeat signal and reduce sampling blind spots. Postmortem scheduled.
notes: This ticket focuses on production dedicated pool behavior. Similar small-stream overlap patterns have been observed previously but not with the same sidecar heartbeat characteristic. Keep this ticket linked to INT-2201 for sidecar stability work.
